parsed.explanation: The combined operative regime exposes travellers: the interior ministry may refuse entry or remove anyone deemed to disturb public order or morality, and rights organisations document deportation of foreign nationals merely suspected of being gay or trans, with no charge upheld (cases to 2022). No statute names homosexual conduct, yet morality/sex-work provisions carry prison sentences, with the financial-exchange requirement removed since the 1970s; police run dating-app entrapment targeting transgender women, with blackmail, arrests, coerced anal examinations and violence in stations. Media incitement and doxxing accompanied mass arrests. No anti-discrimination recourse exists; healthcare discrimination is documented as pervasive. No trans-specific border-marker protocol, homicide rate, or post-2017 forced-examination case is documented — an evidence gap, not safety. No capital or lethal state pathway is shown, which keeps this above the 0.15 anchors.

entry_documents.exposure: Interior ministry may deny entry or deport anyone 'disturbing public order and morality'; 12 documented incidents (2018-2022) plus rights-organisation records show removal of foreign nationals suspected of being gay or trans without any upheld charge.
entry_documents.protection: Not documented. No appeal or screening safeguard for affected travellers is described.
entry_documents.interaction: Decision rests with the same ministry whose police conduct the entrapment operations; no court or independent check is documented before removal.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Dating-app entrapment with fake accounts targeting transgender women; blackmail, arrests, coerced anal examinations, beatings and continuing violations inside police stations; 2017 wave of at least 84 arrests with forced testing.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Not documented. Some 2014 bathhouse defendants were acquitted, showing occasional judicial reversal, but no operative safeguard.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Police are both investigator and documented abuser; acquittals came after custody, so the exposure is already incurred.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Morality and sex-work provisions applied through economic courts now explicitly criminalise habitual conduct, carrying prison sentences; custody abuse documented.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Not documented. No custody-placement, examination or complaint protocol for trans detainees appears.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Prosecutorial reading of the 1961 law plus penal code reaches conduct police observe or elicit; no identity-specific charge is needed for exposure.

care_services.exposure: Policy institute and rights organisations record pervasive gender-identity discrimination in healthcare and persistent barriers to equitable services; no anti-discrimination protection in services.
care_services.interaction: Without a recourse statute, refusal at a clinic leaves the traveller dependent on staff discretion mid-journey.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Media regulator barred LGBT visibility (2017); television hosts incited violence and doxxed flag-displayers, feeding arrests; a presenter collaborated in the 2014 raid; officials frame queer people as moral offenders.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Not documented. Parties and NGOs do not publicly defend LGBT rights.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official and media framing licenses police action and private denunciation, raising the chance that a stranger reports a traveller.

minors_guardians.exposure: A minor travelling with a guardian falls under the same removal power if perceived as queer; family law is religious and marriage is restricted to man and woman.
minors_guardians.interaction: No age-specific safeguard is documented; a guardian's own perceived status compounds the family's removal risk.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Documented incitement, doxxing and mob-adjacent hostility; police documented as perpetrators rather than protectors, with authorities 'turning a blind eye'.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Not documented as operating. Acquittals show courts can reject charges but not that police protect victims.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: A traveller reporting harassment risks exposing themselves to the same officers documented conducting entrapment.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No anti-discrimination law on any SOGIESC ground; removal requires no conviction; legal gender recognition actively closed by a December 2024 nationwide directive.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Occasional acquittals (2014 raid) indicate courts sometimes act, but no working remedy for travellers is documented.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Oversight exists on paper only in the record; the enforcement agency is the same body applying the morality removal power.

anchor_checks.comparison: Vellandra's exclusion is administrative removal without arrest. Here removal coexists with de facto criminalisation carrying prison terms, forced anal examinations in custody and station violence, so this jurisdiction sits materially below that anchor.

Kestrel Isles' secondary screening ends in refused admission with written reasons and an appeal desk. Here no remedy is documented, entrapment targets trans women, and custody abuse is recorded — well below.
Meridia has trained border officers, tribunal appeals, compensation and brief detention. Nothing comparable exists here: no appeal, no counsel access, no anti-discrimination recourse — far below.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime is a chain, not isolated rules: an interior-ministry morality-removal power at the border, a prosecutorial reading of the 1961 sex-work law that reaches habitual conduct, and police entrapment on dating apps aimed specifically at transgender women. Once a traveller is flagged, custody abuse and coerced examinations are documented, with no anti-discrimination statute and no working remedy; courts occasionally acquit but only after exposure. Counterweights — no explicit criminalisation of trans identity, no documented lethal pathway, a 2014 acquittal and 2022 as the last recorded deportations — are real but do not offset the traveller-facing removal-plus-custody chain.
